status: AI linguistic adjudication, recorded with model identities hidden; not independent human validation
method: All 132 packet rows were inspected. Equal candidate texts receive equal linguistic judgments. Formatting wrappers are assessed separately from extracted and accepted text. Reference judgments were frozen first; user examples and historic documentation limit blindness. Correct minimal correction includes a correct no-op on clean input, explicitly marked correct preservation, because the requested eight-label taxonomy lacks that successful outcome.

routineRules.exactProposedRepair: Correct minimal correction: all annotated defects repaired, original factual content and tense intent retained, no additional wording change. For nl-12/en-04 this includes the reference-first alternatives; for en-05/en-09 U+2019 is a legitimate contraction apostrophe.
routineRules.unchangedError: Incorrect or incomplete correction: the input's annotated defect remains under the stated standard-prose policy.
routineRules.unchangedClean: Correct minimal correction, subtype correct preservation: no edit was needed or supplied. This is not counted as a corrected error or suggested edit.

B003.label: Grammatically correct with altered meaning
B003.reason: vergader ruimte denotes a meeting room; vergadering denotes a meeting. Reserving a meeting is not the same proposition as reserving the room. The compound-spelling repair should retain ruimte.

B073.label: Incorrect or incomplete correction
B073.reason: dat de afspraak morgen vindt plaats retains main-clause placement inside a subordinate clause; standard Dutch requires plaatsvindt at the end.

B039.label: Unnecessary change to already-correct text
B039.reason: start was correct; startt introduces a third-person verb spelling error. Date, time and identifiers are retained.

B002.label: Unnecessary change to already-correct text
B002.reason: HTTP 404 can be returned as a status without an article. een is grammatically defensible through an understood status/error noun but is unnecessary in this correct technical sentence.

B122.label: Unnecessary change to already-correct text
B122.reason: Same article addition as B002: no linguistic error required repair, even if the output can be read as grammatical.

B082.label: Protected-content violation
B082.reason: Plain-text source URL is turned into Markdown with a duplicated URL and delimiters. The destination is unchanged, but literal protected-content/format preservation fails. Rejected by validator; accepted text is unchanged and safe.

B107.label: Protected-content violation
B107.reason: Same duplicated Markdown URL transformation as B082. This is a raw surface violation, not evidence of a changed destination. Rejected; accepted text is unchanged.

B124.label: Protected-content violation
B124.reason: Same duplicated Markdown URL transformation as B082. Rejected; accepted text is unchanged.

B085.label: Protected-content violation
B085.reason: OAuth2 becomes OAuth 2.0, changing protected identifier and numeric form. Could denote related technology, but such normalization is unauthorized. Rejected; accepted text unchanged.

B104.label: Protected-content violation
B104.reason: Raw/extracted OAuth2 becomes OAuth 2, changing the literal identifier. The whitespace-only early return emits zero edits, so accepted text actually preserves OAuth2. This is a raw-proposal and trace-observability issue, not an accepted identifier violation.

B119.label: Unnecessary change to already-correct text
B119.reason: team Atlas is already valid Dutch. Adding het is optional phrasing and should not be counted as a necessary proofreading repair.

B126.label: Unnecessary change to already-correct text
B126.reason: Same optional het insertion as B119; original is correct and meaning is substantially retained.

B015.label: Incorrect or incomplete correction
B015.reason: has sent repairs agreement and participle but leaves present perfect with definite finished-time yesterday in this isolated standard-prose context.

B020.label: Grammatically acceptable but semantically ambiguous
B020.reason: had sent is grammatical with an implicit past reference point but introduces a temporal relation not established by the source. Do not equate it automatically with sent; independent human context review required.

B050.label: Grammatically acceptable but semantically ambiguous
B050.reason: Same past-perfect ambiguity as B020. No automatic full repair credit in the strict proposal; no assertion that the sentence is ungrammatical.

B008.label: Requires independent human review
B008.reason: Raw response first repeats the incorrect sentence, then supplies the correct There are sentence in a note. It contains a correct answer but does not unambiguously deliver the requested single corrected passage. The parser selects the incorrect first sentence. This is a response-format/extraction issue, not a missing gold alternative.

B058.label: Protected-content violation
B058.reason: node-04 becomes node 04, altering an exact technical identifier. Removing the hyphen can change a host/resource name. Validator accepts the change: demonstrated safety-coverage gap.

B110.label: Protected-content violation
B110.reason: Plain-text URL is duplicated into Markdown, as in the Dutch URL cases. Rejected by the validator; accepted text unchanged.

B115.label: Protected-content violation
B115.reason: Same duplicated Markdown URL transformation as B110. Rejected; accepted text unchanged.

B070.label: Protected-content violation
B070.reason: OAuth2 becomes OAuth 2.0, changing a protected technical identifier and numeric form. Rejected; accepted text unchanged.
